'''Richard Anthony Lewis Jones''' (born 1961)<ref name="whoswho" /><ref name=loc/> <small>[[Fellow of the Institute of Physics|FInstP]] [[Learned Society of Wales|FLSW]]</small> {{post-nominals|FRS}}<ref name="frs">{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/richard-jones-11705/|title=Professor Richard Jones FRS|author=Anon|year=2012|website=royalsociety.org|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170629024539/https://royalsociety.org/people/richard-jones-11705/|archive-date=29 June 2017}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{blockquote|"All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]." --{{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161111170346/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/|title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies|date=2016-11-11}}}}</ref> is professor of Materials Physics and Innovation Policy at the [[University of Manchester]] having been professor of [[physics]] at the [[University of Sheffield]] until 2020.<ref name="sheffield">{{cite web|url=https://www.sheffield.ac.uk/physics/contacts/richard-jones|title=Richard Jones – Contacts – Physics and Astronomy – The University of Sheffield|first=University of|last=Sheffield|publisher=University of Sheffield}}</ref><ref name="gs">{{Google scholar id}}</ref><ref name="scopus">{{Scopus id}}</ref><ref name=soft>{{cite web|url=http://www.softmachines.org|title=Soft Machines – Some personal views on nanotechnology, science and science policy from Richard Jones|website=softmachines.org}}</ref>

== Education ==
Jones was educated at [[Denstone College]]<ref name=whoswho>{{Who's Who|author=Anon|year=2017|title=Jones, Prof. Richard Anthony Lewis|id=U151439|edition=online |doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U151439|location=Oxford}}</ref> and [[St Catharine's College, Cambridge]], where he studied the [[Natural Sciences Tripos]] and was awarded a Bachelor of Arts degree in Physics 1983.<ref name="whoswho" /> He continued his study at the [[University of Cambridge]] where his PhD investigated diffusion in [[polymer blend]]s.<ref name="raljphd">{{cite thesis|last=Jones|first=Richard Anthony Lewis|title=Mutual diffusion in miscible polymer blends|year=1987|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Cambridge|url=https://copac.jisc.ac.uk/id/27100145?style=html|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.233254}}|website=jisc.ac.uk|oclc=499164519}}</ref>

== Career and research ==
After [[postdoctoral research]] at [[Cornell University]], he was appointed a lecturer at the University of Cambridge based at the [[Cavendish Laboratory]]<ref name="whoswho" /> and in 1998 was appointed a professor at the University of Sheffield.<ref name=about>{{cite web|url=http://www.softmachines.org/wordpress/?page_id=333|title=About Richard Jones – Soft Machines|website=softmachines.org|date=29 October 2011 }}</ref>

Jones' research<ref name="gs"/><ref name="scopus"/> investigates the physics of [[Polymer]]s and [[Biopolymer]]s at [[Surface science|surfaces]] and [[Interface (matter)|interfaces]], with implications for polymer blends.<ref name="frs" /><ref name=scm/> He pioneered the use of [[ion beam]] methods to study the segregation of one component to the surface of a blend.<ref name="frs" /> This in turn led to experiments on [[capillary wave]] broadening of interfaces, using [[Neutron reflector|neutron reflectivity]].<ref name="frs" /> His experiments on the thickness-dependence of [[Glass transition]]s<ref name="KeddieJones1994">{{cite journal|last1=Keddie|first1=J. L|last2=Jones|first2=R. A. L|last3=Cory|first3=R. A|title=Size-Dependent Depression of the Glass Transition Temperature in Polymer Films|journal=Europhysics Letters|volume=27|issue=1|year=1994|pages=59–64|issn=0295-5075|doi=10.1209/0295-5075/27/1/011|bibcode=1994EL.....27...59K |s2cid=250841160 }}</ref> in [[thin film]]s has stimulated a new research field.<ref name="frs" /><ref name="JonesNorton1991">{{cite journal|last1=Jones|first1=Richard A. L.|last2=Norton|first2=Laura J.|last3=Kramer|first3=Edward J.|last4=Bates|first4=Frank S.|last5=Wiltzius|first5=Pierre|title=Surface-directed spinodal decomposition|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=66|issue=10|year=1991|pages=1326–1329|issn=0031-9007|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.66.1326|pmid=10043177 |bibcode=1991PhRvL..66.1326J }}</ref> He has extended his studies to the [[Denaturation (biochemistry)|denaturation of proteins]] at interfaces, demonstrating how the surface [[Hydrophile|hydrophilicity]] has a strong effect, with implications for problems ranging from fouling to disease.<ref name="frs" /><ref name="HowseJones2007">{{cite journal|last1=Howse|first1=Jonathan R.|last2=Jones|first2=Richard A. L.|last3=Ryan|first3=Anthony J.|last4=Gough|first4=Tim|last5=Vafabakhsh|first5=Reza|last6=Golestanian|first6=Ramin|title=Self-Motile Colloidal Particles: From Directed Propulsion to Random Walk|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=99|issue=4|year=2007|article-number=048102 |issn=0031-9007|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.99.048102|pmid=17678409 |arxiv=0706.4406|bibcode=2007PhRvL..99d8102H |s2cid=16932092 }}</ref>

In 2018 he co-authored ''The Biomedical Bubble''<ref name=bubble>{{cite web|url=https://www.nesta.org.uk/report/biomedical-bubble|website=nesta.org.uk|publisher=[[Nesta (charity)|Nesta]]|year=2018|title=The Biomedical Bubble|first1=Richard A. J.|last1=Jones|first2=James|last2=Wilsdon}}</ref> with {{ill|James Wilsdon|qid=Q54202734}}, which argued that [[United Kingdom Research and Innovation]] (UKRI) needs a greater diversity of priorities, politics, places and people.<ref name="lancet">{{Cite journal|author=Anon|year=2018|title=Editorial: UK life science research: time to burst the biomedical bubble|journal=[[The Lancet]]|volume=392|issue=10143|page=187|doi=10.1016/S0140-6736(18)31609-X|pmid=30043738|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name="ft">{{cite web|url=https://www.ft.com/content/92ace4de-88e9-11e8-affd-da9960227309|work=[[Financial Times]]|title=Britain must stop inflating the biomedical bubble|last=Ahuja|first=Anjana|author-link=Anjana Ahuja|year=2018}} {{subscription required}}</ref><ref name=gordian>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/political-science/2018/jul/12/its-time-to-burst-the-biomedical-bubble-in-uk-research|work=[[The Guardian]]|year=2018|first1=Richard A. J.|last1=Jones|first2=James|last2=Wilsdon|title=It's time to burst the biomedical bubble in UK research}}</ref><ref name=wonk>{{cite web|url=https://wonkhe.com/blogs/rethinking-the-life-sciences-strategy/|website=wonkhe.com|title=Rethinking the life sciences strategy|year=2018|first1=Richard A. J.|last1=Jones|first2=James|last2=Wilsdon}}</ref><ref name=mrc>{{cite news|first=Fiona|last=Watt|year=2018|author-link=Fiona Watt|url=https://www.insight.mrc.ac.uk/2018/08/09/popping-the-bubble/|website=insight.mrc.ac.uk|title=Popping the bubble|publisher=[[Medical Research Council (United Kingdom)|Medical Research Council]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180910150804/https://www.insight.mrc.ac.uk/2018/08/09/popping-the-bubble/|archive-date=10 September 2018}}</ref>

In 2020, Jones moved to Manchester.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.manchester.ac.uk/discover/news/new-chair-in-materials-physics-and-innovation-policy/ |title=New Chair in Materials Physics and Innovation Policy |publisher=University of Manchester |access-date=14 April 2020}}</ref>

=== Awards and honours ===
Jones was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) in 2006 for "substantial contributions to the improvement of natural knowledge".<ref name="frs" />

In 2008 he won the [[Institute of Physics]] [[David Tabor Medal and Prize]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.iop.org/about/awards/subject/tabor/tabor-medallists/page_38605.html |title=2008 Tabor Medal and Prize |publisher=Institute of Physics |access-date=23 December 2019}}</ref>

In 2021, Jones was elected a [[Learned Society of Wales|Fellow of the Learned Society of Wales]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wales |first=The Learned Society of |title=Richard A.L. Jones |url=https://www.learnedsociety.wales/fellow/richard-a-l-jones/ |access-date=2023-08-30 |website=The Learned Society of Wales |language=en-US}}</ref>
